body: I was not able to reproduce the problem unfortunately.  Could you please edit `io.netty.util.internal.QueueFactory.createQueue()` to make it return other queue implementation such as a `LinkedBlockingQueue` or a `java.util.concurrent.LinkedTransferQueue`?

Upon retrying, I too was running into some difficulty in reproducing it. I'm seeing it manifest itself in different ways on Mac vs Linux (don't have Windows handy)). On the Mac the problem actually shows up as the process utilizing more CPU (when the Netty server process is idle) as reported by top. However, on Linux there's a spike and plateau of elevated context switches but the CPU utilization remains at 0% and load average stays at 0.00. Here are the steps by which I am able to consistently reproduce it.

Some context
- The Mac system
  - Darwin elcapitan.local 11.3.0 Darwin Kernel Version 11.3.0: Thu Jan 12 18:47:41 PST 2012; root:xnu-1699.24.23~1/RELEASE_X86_64 x86_64
  - java version "1.7.0_04-ea" Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 1.7.0_04-ea-b14) Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 23.0-b16, mixed mode)```
- The Linux system
  - Linux firebase-staging-ignite 2.6.18-308.8.2.el5xen #1 SMP Tue Jun 12 10:39:28 EDT 2012 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
  - java version "1.7.0_03" Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment (build 1.7.0_03-b04) Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM (build 22.1-b02, mixed mode)```
- Netty build
  - Master from earlier today, July 25 ( 137525d4c5207b2ee8ab416dc4a2546de8c6c50a ).
  - Modified `example/src/main/java/io/netty/example/http/websocketx/server/WebSocketServerInitializer.java` as per above in change the pipeline to utilize a DefaultEventExecutor.
  - Modified `all/pom.xml` to not exclude examples in final JAR (just to make the following command lines a bit easier to run).
    Built using Apache Maven 3.0.3 (r1075438; 2011-02-28 09:31:09-0800)

Reproducing the issue:
In terminal window 1, start up the server:

```
    $ java -cp netty-4.0.0.Alpha2-SNAPSHOT.jar io.netty.example.http.websocketx.server.WebSocketServer
```

In terminal window 2, observe the system/process with no clients/activity:

```
    ### On a Mac, observe 0% CPU and 0.00 load, etc
    $ top -pid `ps auxw|grep WebSocketServer|grep -v grep|awk '{print $2}'`
    ### On Linux, observe context switched (on my system, this is about 250/sec)
    $ while [ : ]; do CURR=`cat /proc/stat |grep ctxt|awk '{print $2}'`; echo `expr $CURR - $PREV`; PREV=$CURR; sleep 1;  done
```

In terminal window 3, throw some work at the server:

```
    $ for moo in {1..50}; do java -cp netty-4.0.0.Alpha2-SNAPSHOT.jar io.netty.example.http.websocketx.client.WebSocketClient 1> /dev/null 2> /dev/null ; echo $moo ; done
```

At this point, once the clients have completed (and there isn't any new work coming into our server), you should see in terminal window 2 that the Mac's top reporting a steady 10% of CPU being utilized and Linux doing about 4000 ctx switches/second.  Even after 10 minutes of all the clinets having been shutdown, I'm not seeing these numbers come down.

I tried the alternative queue implementations with no luck.

I believe because each event executor thread wakes up every 6 milliseconds, which is roughly about 170 wake-ups per second per thread.  Each thread wakes up to check if there is any scheduled tasks and to add them to the task queue.  Probably 6 ms is way too low and we need better ways to handle this issue.

To confirm my assumption, could you please increase `SingleThreadEventExecutor.SCHEDULE_CHECK_INTERVAL` to a larger value and see if it makes any difference?
The reason why context switching frequency was not high in the beginning is because the threads are started on demand.
Thanks for the explanation! I'll continue to tune and monitor this area of our code.
I noticed you closed this issue.  Does it mean you are fine with the elevated context switching?  Please feel free to reopen this issue if you think it's still a problem for you.

I'm not necessarily fine with it, but your explanation of it sounds reasonable :) It's definitely going to impact our ability to do capacity planning if we can't get visibility into how bogged down the system actually is. We just rolled it out to production and will continue to experiment with the settings you mentioned. I'll re-open it if I can come up with any concrete problems. Thanks again for your help and insight!

Reopening because this seems to impact the performance badly when a user uses a `DefaultEventExecutor` with the large number of threads in his/her pipeline.  Instead of making every thread check scheduled events, we should use a dedicated `ScheduledExecutorService` that wakes up the event loop.
The context switching should be significantly lower than before now.  @vikrum, could you please confirm?
Trustin, I just got back in town. Will give it a whirl and let you know.
which release is this issue fixed? I tried 3.5.7 and the context switching are even higher than 3.5.3 when using netty for  client connections.
@gauravsri, this is only for 4.x alpha releases, which has a rewritten event loop.
@vikrum Any updates on this?  Not rushing though. :-)

issue.title: WebSocketClientHandshaker is broken.

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body: The WebSocket client example does not work as reported in #473.  It turns out that the WebSocketClientHandshaker removes HttpRequestDecoder too soon.  Also, the example itself sends the frame too soon.
